evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with chronic widespread pain, fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and cognitive symptoms in primary care, rheumatology or the emergency department: criteria-based diagnosis, avoidance of missed alternative diagnoses, a graduated multidisciplinary plan (education, exercise, psychological therapy, selected medicines, multimodal rehabilitation), medicine doses with cautions, and review. Diagnostic criteria and graduated management come from the 2016 revisions to the 2010/2011 fibromyalgia diagnostic criteria (Wolfe 2016) and the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) 2017 recommendations; drug doses and contraindications come from the Saudi Ministry of Health (MOH) Neuropathic Pain protocol. No Saudi fibromyalgia guideline was found. Children, juvenile fibromyalgia and pregnancy are outside this topic.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health, Saudi Health Council or Saudi rheumatology society fibromyalgia guideline was found or opened; the authority is therefore not MOH. The MOH Neuropathic Pain protocol (Protocol-009) lists drug doses for neuropathic pain and does not mention fibromyalgia.

The MOH Neuropathic Pain protocol is not a fibromyalgia protocol; its dose table is used here only for the dose of drugs that EULAR recommends for fibromyalgia, and the fibromyalgia indication itself comes from EULAR.

The EULAR text was read through a journal page extract that did not include Table 3 or Figure 2; the recommendation strengths and the statements about amitriptyline 25 mg and duloxetine 60 mg come from the narrative, and the four-stage flow chart was not read in full.

No source opened gives a list of blood tests to exclude other diagnoses; the exclusion panel and the red-flag list are added clinical practice and are labelled as such. The Wolfe criteria state only that a fibromyalgia diagnosis does not exclude other clinically important illness.

Pregabalin renal dosing, pregnancy and breastfeeding advice, duloxetine starting doses in mg beyond the MOH table, and amitriptyline interaction and pregnancy information were not found (NHS amitriptyline-for-pain pages could not be opened); check the product monograph.

The MOH table prints capsaicin 8% patch as not available and lidocaine as gel in the local formulary; both are omitted because EULAR rates capsaicin weak against for fibromyalgia. The MOH page header lists a medicine checklist (cannabis extract, lacosamide, lamotrigine, levetiracetam, morphine, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, hydroxyurea) as 'should not be on' before starting neuropathic pain treatment; its purpose is unclear and it is not applied here.
Gabapentin appears in the MOH table with doses, but EULAR rates it research only for fibromyalgia, so it is not included as a regimen.
Pregabalin and tramadol availability and controlled-medicine rules in Saudi Arabia were not verified.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

Source pages were read through automated page extraction (MOH PDF converted to text; EULAR, Wolfe and NHS pages summarised by a page reader) rather than page by page in the originals, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition of widespread pain with fatigue, waking unrefreshed and cognitive symptoms, diagnosed by symptom criteria rather than a test (Wolfe 2016). The diagnosis is valid irrespective of other diagnoses and does not exclude other clinically important illness, so coexisting inflammatory, thyroid or mood disease must still be sought and treated (Wolfe 2016, Table 3). Management is graduated: education and non-drug therapy first, then tailored psychological, drug or multimodal rehabilitation steps if the first stage fails (EULAR). Exercise is the only therapy-based recommendation rated strong; most other options are weak (EULAR). Neuropathic-pain drugs (pregabalin, duloxetine, amitriptyline) act on central pain pathways; their fibromyalgia role is for severe pain or sleep disturbance (EULAR).

symptoms: Widespread pain for at least 3 months.
Headache, lower abdominal pain or cramps, low mood (Symptom Severity Scale items).
physicalSigns: Tenderness over multiple body regions without joint swelling (added clinical observation).
Normal neurological examination apart from pain-related guarding (added clinical observation).
Low mood or anxiety affecting coping.
redFlags: Fever, unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or a new rash: look for infection, malignancy or inflammatory disease before labelling fibromyalgia (added clinical practice; see gaps).
Objective joint swelling, morning stiffness longer than an hour, or abnormal inflammatory markers: assess for an inflammatory arthritis (added clinical practice).
Focal weakness, sensory loss, bladder or bowel change: neurological emergency pathway (added clinical practice).
Suicidal thoughts or severe depression: same-day mental health assessment (added clinical practice).
Severe disability from pain: EULAR recommends multimodal rehabilitation.
Starting duloxetine with a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (within 14 days), linezolid or intravenous methylene blue is contraindicated (MOH).
precipitants: Poor sleep and stress may worsen symptoms (added clinical observation).
Coexisting depression or anxiety (Wolfe symptom severity item).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Objective joint swelling and raised inflammatory markers; fibromyalgia can coexist (Wolfe 2016).

differentials.condition: Hypothyroidism and other metabolic causes of fatigue and aches
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Abnormal thyroid stimulating hormone or other laboratory abnormality (added clinical practice).
Primary low mood and loss of interest; treat both (added clinical practice).
Pain in a nerve distribution with sensory signs; the MOH Neuropathic Pain protocol applies (MOH).
Onset after starting a drug such as a statin; creatine kinase may be raised (added clinical practice).

clinicalManagement.title: First minutes: widespread pain presentation
actions: Rate pain on the 0 to 10 scale (1 to 3 mild, 4 to 6 moderate, 7 to 10 severe) and give analgesia within 30 minutes of presentation (MOH Neuropathic Pain protocol, header).
Screen for red flags (fever, weight loss, joint swelling, focal neurological signs, bladder or bowel change, suicidal thoughts) and pursue them first (added clinical practice).
Check heart rate, blood pressure and temperature before labelling the pain as fibromyalgia (added clinical practice).

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnose by criteria
actions: Count painful areas (WPI, 0 to 19) and score the SSS (0 to 12). Diagnose if WPI 7 or more with SSS 5 or more, or WPI 4 to 6 with SSS 9 or more, with generalised pain in at least 4 of 5 regions, present for at least 3 months (Wolfe 2016).
Diagnose promptly: EULAR states that optimal management requires prompt diagnosis, with a full assessment of pain, function and the psychosocial context.
Check thyroid stimulating hormone, blood count and inflammatory markers for coexisting illness (panel added).

clinicalManagement.title: Stage 1: education and exercise
actions: Explain the diagnosis, give written information and agree goals with shared decision-making (EULAR).
Prescribe regular exercise; it is the only strong recommendation (EULAR).
Offer hydrotherapy, acupuncture, meditative movement or mindfulness-based stress reduction as weak-for options (EULAR).
Avoid chiropractic, homeopathy, guided imagery (strong against) and biofeedback, capsaicin, hypnotherapy, massage, S-adenosylmethionine (weak against) (EULAR).

clinicalManagement.title: Stage 2: tailored further therapy if no response
clinicalManagement.timeframe: After an adequate trial of stage 1
actions: Psychological therapy (cognitive behavioural therapy) for mood disorders or unhelpful coping strategies (EULAR).
Medicines for severe pain or sleep disturbance: duloxetine, pregabalin or tramadol for pain; low-dose amitriptyline, cyclobenzaprine or pregabalin for sleep (EULAR; doses from the MOH table below).

Do not use strong opioids, corticosteroids, growth hormone or sodium oxybate (strong against), nor non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, monoamine oxidase inhibitors or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (weak against) (EULAR).

clinicalManagement.title: Review
actions: Repeat WPI, SSS and the pain score at each visit; stop a medicine that is not helping; amitriptyline benefit at 25 mg a day was seen at 6 to 8 weeks but not at 12 weeks in trials (EULAR).
Refer to rheumatology or a pain service if the diagnosis is uncertain, there is severe disability or two stages have failed (added clinical practice).

regimens.indication: Fibromyalgia with severe pain (EULAR weak for; 60 mg a day effective, 20 to 30 mg not significant)
regimens.dose: MOH: start 20 to 30 mg a day, or 60 mg a day; effective 60 to 120 mg a day in divided doses; titrate 60 mg up to 60 mg twice a day. EULAR: 60 mg a day for fibromyalgia
regimens.duration: Continue if pain improves; review at 4 to 12 weeks; reduce gradually over several weeks or months when stopping (NHS)
adjustments: Hepatic impairment and severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease: contraindicated (MOH).
NHS: the dose may be raised after a week or more; capsules swallowed whole.
Pregnancy, breastfeeding and older-adult dosing not stated in the sources opened.
monitoring: Pain score and Symptom Severity Scale at each review; liver function; stop gradually to avoid withdrawal (NHS).
contraindications: MOH: monoamine oxidase inhibitor within 14 days of stopping it, or starting a monoamine oxidase inhibitor within 5 days of stopping duloxetine; linezolid or intravenous methylene blue; hepatic impairment; severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease; uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma; thioridazine or potent CYP1A2 inhibitors.

regimens.indication: Fibromyalgia with severe pain or sleep disturbance (EULAR weak for)
regimens.dose: MOH: 150 mg a day in two or three divided doses; increase to 300 mg a day after 3 to 7 days; effective 300 to 600 mg a day
regimens.frequency: Two or three divided doses a day (slow-release once daily, NHS)
regimens.duration: Continue if effective; reduce gradually when stopping, to avoid withdrawal symptoms and seizures (NHS)
adjustments: Kidney or elderly adjustment: not stated in the MOH table; NHS says it might not be suitable over age 65 and for kidney disease; check the product monograph.
Missed dose: take when remembered unless within 2 hours of the next dose (NHS).
Pregnancy and breastfeeding advice not found; discuss with the prescriber.
monitoring: Sedation, dizziness, weight gain, breathing problems; mood and misuse risk; review need at each visit (NHS).
contraindications: Previous allergic reaction to pregabalin; history of medicine misuse or addiction; breathing problems; heart disease; liver or kidney disease; controlled sodium diet (NHS). Not suitable under 18 (NHS).

regimens.indication: Fibromyalgia sleep disturbance or pain at low dose (EULAR weak for; 25 mg a day benefit, 50 mg a day no added efficacy)
regimens.dose: MOH: start 10 to 25 mg a day; increase 10 to 25 mg every 3 to 7 days as tolerated; effective 25 to 75 mg a day; above 100 mg a day only with caution. EULAR: 25 mg a day
regimens.duration: Review at 6 to 8 weeks; stop if no benefit (EULAR trials showed benefit at 6 to 8 weeks, not at 12 weeks)
adjustments: Severe hepatic impairment or acute heart failure: contraindicated (MOH).
Older adults, renal impairment and pregnancy: not stated in the MOH table; use the lowest dose and check the product monograph.
monitoring: Sedation, anticholinergic effects, heart rhythm and blood pressure if cardiac risk; suicidal thoughts (added clinical practice).
contraindications: MOH: severe liver impairment; acute heart failure.

regimens.indication: Severe fibromyalgia pain when acute rescue therapy is needed (EULAR weak for; MOH: consider only for acute rescue)
regimens.dose: MOH: start 50 mg a day, increase weekly by 50 mg a day; immediate release 25 to 50 mg every 6 hours as needed, up to 50 to 100 mg every 4 to 6 hours, maximum 400 mg a day; extended release 100 mg once daily, titrate by 100 mg a day every 5 days, maximum 300 mg a day
regimens.frequency: Every 4 to 6 hours as needed (immediate release); once daily (extended release)
adjustments: Contraindicated in severe renal or hepatic impairment, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and under 12 years (MOH).
Older-adult dose reduction is not stated in the MOH table.
monitoring: Sedation, respiratory depression, seizure risk, dependence.
contraindications: MOH: severe renal or severe hepatic impairment; status asthmaticus, chronic obstructive airway disease, acute or severe bronchial asthma; acute respiratory depression; hypercapnia; delirium tremens; seizure disorder; severe central nervous system depression; raised intracranial pressure; head injury; suspected surgical abdomen; acute intoxication with ethanol, hypnotics, centrally acting analgesics, opioids or psychotropic drugs; breastfeeding; pregnancy; labour; children under 12; gastrointestinal obstruction; use with a monoamine oxidase inhibitor or within 14 days after.

medicationPlan.note: Fibromyalgia drugs are chosen from the EULAR recommendations; the dose tables, titration and contraindications are from the MOH Neuropathic Pain protocol, which does not itself address fibromyalgia. Pregabalin renal dosing and pregnancy advice were not found. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Widespread Pain Index (WPI) 7 or more with Symptom Severity Scale (SSS) 5 or more, or WPI 4 to 6 with SSS 9 or more (Wolfe 2016, Table 3).
Pain in at least 4 of 5 body regions; jaw, chest and abdominal pain are not counted in the generalised pain definition (Wolfe 2016, Table 3).
Symptoms present at a similar level for at least 3 months (Wolfe 2016, abstract and Table 3).

Fatigue, waking unrefreshed and cognitive symptoms each scored 0 to 3 (0 to 9), plus headache, lower abdominal pain or cramps and depression each scored 0 or 1 (0 to 3): total 0 to 12 (Wolfe 2016, Table 3).
1 to 3 mild; 4 to 6 moderate; 7 to 10 severe (MOH Neuropathic Pain protocol, Page 6).
Drugs for severe pain or sleep disturbance after non-drug measures: duloxetine, pregabalin or tramadol for pain; amitriptyline, cyclobenzaprine or pregabalin for sleep.

teaching.scope: Adult with chronic widespread pain, fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and cognitive symptoms in primary care, rheumatology or the emergency department: criteria-based diagnosis, avoidance of missed alternative diagnoses, a graduated multidisciplinary plan (education, exercise, psychological therapy, selected medicines, multimodal rehabilitation), medicine doses with cautions, and review. Diagnostic criteria and graduated management come from the 2016 revisions to the 2010/2011 fibromyalgia diagnostic criteria (Wolfe 2016) and the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) 2017 recommendations; drug doses and contraindications come from the Saudi Ministry of Health (MOH) Neuropathic Pain protocol. No Saudi fibromyalgia guideline was found. Children, juvenile fibromyalgia and pregnancy are outside this topic.
learningObjectives: Diagnose by WPI and SSS criteria and still look for coexisting disease.
Start with education and exercise; add psychological or drug therapy for those who do not improve.
Use pregabalin, duloxetine or low-dose amitriptyline only for severe pain or sleep disturbance, and stop what does not work.
pitfalls: Labelling widespread pain as fibromyalgia without checking for inflammatory, thyroid or neurological disease.
Giving duloxetine with linezolid or a monoamine oxidase inhibitor.
keyPoints: WPI 7 or more with SSS 5 or more, or WPI 4 to 6 with SSS 9 or more, for at least 3 months.
Exercise is the only strong recommendation; strong opioids and corticosteroids are recommended against.
Duloxetine 60 mg a day; amitriptyline 25 mg a day; pregabalin 300 to 600 mg a day (MOH range).

patientEducation: Fibromyalgia is real, common and not dangerous to the joints; the plan is gradual improvement in function, not a cure.
Regular, graded exercise is the most effective treatment; start low and build up.
Do not stop duloxetine or pregabalin suddenly; report low mood or suicidal thoughts.
lifestyleAndDiet: Regular exercise, sleep routine, pacing of activities; reduce stress.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; rheumatology; pain medicine; physiotherapy; psychologist for cognitive behavioural therapy; occupational therapy; clinical pharmacist; mental health service if depression.
dischargeCriteria: Discharge from emergency care once red flags are excluded, pain is controlled, a medicine plan is explained and follow-up is booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review in 4 to 12 weeks with WPI, SSS and pain score; then every 3 to 6 months; refer to rheumatology or a pain service if the diagnosis is doubtful or disability is severe.
